business_problem: Apna outgrew a monolithic backend and needed an event-driven architecture that could scale its hiring marketplace, power better analytics, and avoid turning a growing platform team into Kafka operators.
solution_summary: Apna moved from a monolithic backend to an event-driven architecture built on Confluent Cloud in GCP. The managed Kafka service became the backbone for real-time microservices that support job matching, search, and community features, while removing the operational burden of scaling brokers in-house. Apna also built a data lakehouse on top of the streaming platform, generating 20 TB of Kafka data per month for faster analytics and more personalized user experiences. Schema Registry governs schemas across those streams, and the MongoDB Kafka connector captures database changes into the lakehouse. With Confluent's out-of-the-box connectors, the team can pipe data from process databases into Kafka and onward to the lake without custom plumbing, which lets developers spend more time on product capabilities such as learning assessments and recommendations.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Provides the managed Kafka backbone for Apna's event-driven microservices and lakehouse pipelines.

solution_components.name: Schema Registry
solution_components.role: Governs schemas for the real-time streams that feed the lakehouse and application services.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Kafka connector
solution_components.role: Captures MongoDB changes into Kafka for downstream lakehouse analytics and personalization.

data_flow: Application and database changes flow through Confluent Cloud into real-time microservices and a lakehouse, where Schema Registry keeps formats consistent and the MongoDB Kafka connector supplies change data for downstream analytics, matching, and recommendation use cases.
business_outcome: Apna scaled its platform with a more stable event-driven backbone, cut delivery time for new solutions, increased reliability, and redirected engineering effort from Kafka operations into new products and user-facing recommendations.
